builds.name: Reference: Ranked mid core
builds.goal: Reference for LeBlanc: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ mid players use most (4,979 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 49.5% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A mobile burst mage who links a marked spell sequence and returns through Distortion to limit retaliation. Chains reward maintaining a tether long enough for delayed control. The current mid provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Luden's Echo → Shadowflame → Rabadon's Deathcap. Electrocute keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Sorcerer's Shoes, Zhonya's Hourglass, Void Staff.
builds.summary: The proven mid baseline: Luden's Echo → Shadowflame → Rabadon's Deathcap, with Electrocute.
testPlan: Play it in mid as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Luden's Echo → Shadowflame → Rabadon's Deathcap) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 49.5% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Luden's Echo → Shadowflame → Rabadon's Deathcap.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.
builds.author: Rift Build Lab ranked data

kitEvidence.formula:
LeBlanc launches a chain that shackles the first enemy hit, dealing [50 / 70 / 90 / 110 / 130 + (0.4) × AP] magic damage and granting True Sight.

If they remain shackled for [1.5] seconds, LeBlanc Roots them for [1.5] seconds and deals an additional [80 / 120 / 160 / 200 / 240 + (0.85) × AP] magic damage.

LeBlanc projects a sigil to an enemy, dealing [65 / 90 / 115 / 140 / 165 + (0.4) × AP] magic damage and marking them for [3.5] seconds.

Damaging the marked enemy with an Ability detonates the sigil, dealing [65 / 90 / 115 / 140 / 165 + (0.4) × AP] magic damage.

If either part kills the target, Leblanc refunds [100]% of the Mana cost and [30]% of this spell's remaining Cooldown.

The initial sigil deals an additional [characterLevelBreakpoints(start=10, perLevel=8, changes=[])] damage to minions.
When LeBlanc drops below 40% Health, she becomes Invisible for 1 second and creates a harmless clone for 8 seconds. LeBlanc can move the clone with the "Alt" key.

LeBlanc dashes then deals [75 / 115 / 155 / 195 / 235 + (0.9) × AP] magic damage to nearby enemies. For [4] seconds after dashing, LeBlanc can Recast.

Recast: LeBlanc returns to her starting location.

LeBlanc mimics her most recent Ability, using it again. The mimicked Ability deals increased damage.

Mimicked Sigil of Malice deals [70 / 150 / 230 + (0.4) × AP] magic damage when applied, and [140 / 300 / 460 + (0.8) × AP] magic damage when consumed.
Mimicked Distortion deals [150 / 315 / 480 + (0.9) × AP] magic damage.
Mimicked Ethereal Chains deals [70 / 150 / 230 + (0.4) × AP] magic damage when shackled and [140 / 300 / 460 + (0.85) × AP] magic damage when Rooting.

builds.name: Chain attack duelist
builds.summary: Test chain attack duelist against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.goal: Test chain attack duelist against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.hypothesis: Ethereal Chains roots only after a 1.5-second tether; Nashor and Dusk and Dawn add magic attack pressure while waiting, then Distortion return offers escape. AP supports the large 0.85 AP root hit, but this route must maintain the chain without substituting attacks for Sigil detonation.
testPlan: Required state: Keep the target tethered and attack safely before returning W.
Compare chain damage and attacks landed during the tether against pure burst.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Short attack range exposes LeBlanc and lowers normal instant burst.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Mirror Image deals no damage and must not receive copied item DPS.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Nashor's Tooth, Dusk and Dawn, Riftmaker, Terminus, Banshee's Veil, Berserker's Greaves. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Survive the engage
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for LeBlanc: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A mobile burst mage who links a marked spell sequence and returns through Distortion to limit retaliation. Chains reward maintaining a tether long enough for delayed control. Compare mark detonation and return-safe spell burst with real attacks between casts. Chains must remain connected; returning through W can end the damage window. A transformed mana shield, stasis and a spell shield may preserve repeat casts.
builds.summary: A transformed mana shield, stasis and a spell shield may preserve repeat casts.
testPlan: Kit question for LeBlanc: Compare mark detonation and return-safe spell burst with real attacks between casts. Chains must remain connected; returning through W can end the damage window.

Start with the early core (Archangel, then the defense matching the opponent) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: A transformed mana shield, stasis and a spell shield may preserve repeat casts. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: LeBlanc projects a sigil, dealing damage and marking the target for 3.5 seconds. Damaging the marked target with an ability detonates the sigil, dealing additional damage. If either part kills the target, Leblanc refunds the Mana cost and part of this spell's remaining Cooldown. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Defensive redundancy can sacrifice too much damage; this is conditional on real threats.

The route fails LeBlanc's stated kit question: Compare mark detonation and return-safe spell burst with real attacks between casts. Chains must remain connected; returning through W can end the damage window.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: Defensive redundancy can sacrifice too much damage; this is conditional on real threats.
Full cost 16,000 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Archangel, then the defense matching the opponent. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Banshee's Veil, Rylai's Crystal Scepter, Void Staff are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.name: Double-chain magic shred
builds.summary: Test double-chain magic shred against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.goal: Test double-chain magic shred against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.hypothesis: E and Mimic E each deliver separate initial and delayed magic hits; Bloodletter and Liandry support sustained tether pressure while Cosmic Drive helps keep both chains attached. Earned Seraph supplies mana and a late defensive shield, trading some assassination power for repeated control.
testPlan: Required state: Attach two chains without losing their delayed roots.
Compare MR stacks and damage over a complete double-chain exchange.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Dashes or shields can break the tether before the important second hits.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: An attack cannot detonate Q's marked sigil, which explicitly requires ability damage.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
